prompt: Create a finished 16:9 handmade paper and card diorama thumbnail, full frame, no border. A London laborer’s rough hands set down one small loaf beside a tiny candle and a folded scrap of linen; a long paper strip of 250 punched wage marks ends before a much longer 333-mark strip, making the shortfall visually legible without extra numerals. One large paper coin balances at the gap. Bold rounded slightly irregular dimensional cut-paper lettering reads exactly “THE YEARLY BILL”. Warm candlelight on the bread, deep slate-blue shadow behind, tactile fibers, layered cut edges, physical contact shadows, strong simple silhouette, rich but controlled detail. Aim attention from the loaf to the coin and the visibly incomplete wage strip. No photoreal people, no modern objects, no extra text, no fake archival look.
visual_intent: Intro object/action: bread, fuel/light and a basic necessity bill meet a finite wage strip. At thumbnail scale the loaf, coin and unfinished strip must read before details; the large phrase supplies the yearly-bill frame, while the title asks the wage-days question.
